newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BIS says Brazil's real is 20 pct overvalued - paper.
newsitem.headline: BIS says Brazil's real is 20 pct overvalued - paper.

text.p: Brazil's real currency is 20 percent overvalued against the dollar according to a report by the Bank of International Settlements (BIS), Jornal do Brasil daily reported on Wednesday.

The BIS report, released Monday in Switzerland, said, "The real currency depreciation has been slow and progressive, slightly below consumer prices, so that in real terms the currency is 20 percent overvalued," the newspaper said.

In an interview to a local magazine published last month, U.S. economist Rudiger Dornbusch, criticizing Brazil's foreign exchange rate policy, said Brazil should speed currency depreciation by about five percent a year for the next five years.
The BIS said Brazil is not the only country facing the problem of an overvalued currency and also cited Argentina, Chile and Colombia in Latin America, Jornal do Brasil said.

The BIS report also said that, among 17 emerging economies, 11 showed higher rates of growth in imports in 1996, the paper said. Also, fourteen of the 17 countries reported current account deficits in their balance of payments, it added.
